draft:
# Schedule a CobaltKey certificate cutover

This advisory is for service owners moving from an accepted certificate to a staged replacement. Treat preparation, schedule acceptance, and activation as distinct events. Staging creates an inactive candidate; it does not begin acceptance of the new certificate. A maintenance record should make clear which of these events has actually occurred.

## Prepare the replacement identity

A replacement candidate is eligible only when its subject identity matches the current certificate's subject identity. Check that relationship when preparing the replacement rather than assuming any otherwise usable certificate belongs to the same service identity.

For validation without candidate creation, run `ckctl stage --check-only` with the certificate input. This option validates the supplied certificate without creating a candidate. Its output is not evidence that a staged candidate exists, and it is not evidence that a candidate has completed a signed probe. Use staging when an inactive candidate is needed for the actual cutover.

## Select the activation window

Supply `--activate-at` as a UTC RFC 3339 timestamp ending in `Z`. At schedule acceptance, the requested activation time must be at least 30 seconds in the future. Exactly 30 seconds is allowed. Judge the lead time at acceptance, rather than assuming a timestamp remains eligible simply because it was far enough ahead when an operator first wrote it down.

The `--overlap` option is measured in seconds. Choose a value greater than 30 and no greater than 300; the lower bound is exclusive. This interval controls how long the old certificate remains accepted after the new certificate begins acceptance. It is separate from the minimum lead time used to decide whether a schedule can be accepted.

## Schedule and probe

After staging, submit the activation schedule. Then complete the successful signed probe before the activation timestamp arrives. The probe is required, but it can be performed after schedule submission as long as it finishes before activation. Record its result so the handoff distinguishes scheduling from verification.

Select the staged certificate for the probe using `candidate_id`, not the active-certificate alias. A result of `probe_status=passed` means that the signed challenge was successfully verified with the staged certificate's public key. A probe of the currently active certificate would not establish that result for the replacement candidate.

## Interpret the overlap boundary

The new certificate begins acceptance at the activation timestamp itself. The old certificate remains accepted during the overlap interval. At `activation_time + overlap`, the old certificate is rejected; that endpoint is not part of its acceptance interval.

For example, activation at 10:00:00Z with an overlap of 60 seconds starts new-certificate acceptance at 10:00:00Z. The old certificate stops being accepted at 10:01:00Z. These times describe certificate acceptance, not a guarantee that every client has refreshed its cached chain.

## Revise a pending schedule

Use `--replace` to supersede an existing pending activation schedule. The option is unavailable at or after the scheduled activation time, so it is a pending-schedule operation rather than a way to reverse a completed activation.

Clients SHOULD refresh cached certificate chains before activation. This is a recommendation, not a validity precondition for the cutover. Include the intended activation time, the overlap duration, and the candidate probe result in the operator handoff so each value retains its separate meaning.
